title: German saucer airframe with boundary-layer suction vents
summary: Jason Jorjani tells of German saucer airframe with boundary-layer suction vents, about 1930s-1940s at Germany, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: So they came up with the idea of creating a saucer-shaped craft that would have suction vents all around it.

plain: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says German engineers of the 1930s and 1940s came up with a saucer-shaped aircraft with suction vents all around its edge. The vents would pull in the thin layer of air that clings to a craft's surface, called the boundary layer. If true, it would mean Germany was designing flying saucers during the Second World War.
